A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same Sparse Attention Vectors (SAVs) work despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments, ablations, transfer tests, and appendix robustness and language-only results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional benchmark and baseline evaluations in Tables 1 and 2.

M1.justification: The centroid-based head selection, majority voting, and optional online-learning algorithm are unchanged. V3 adds a limited task-specific inference adaptation for VizWiz: answerability classification followed by standard response generation (Section 4.2). The local/global classifier terminology does not change the core SAV algorithm.

E1.justification: V3 adds VizWiz, NaturalBench retrieval, SUGARCREPE image-text matching, and ImageNet-1k, Flowers, and CUB classification evaluations. These expand task requirements, populations, and visual domains. Original NaturalBench VQA remains under a more explicit name, and the appendix SST-2 and MNLI evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4o, LLaVA-1.5, InstructBLIP, and generative 4-shot ICL comparisons, while removing the Last L and All L feature baselines. V3 also introduces VQAScore for retrieval comparisons and adds Cross-Modal Adaptation to the existing mean-centroid few-shot SigLIP comparison, moved from v2 Table 5a to v3 Table 2c.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce a 16-way ImageNet protocol, VizWiz answerability classification followed by generation, and VQAScore retrieval scoring. The reported transfer comparison changes its source from MHaluBench to VLGuard. The standard 20 examples per label, 20 selected heads, and four-choice EuroSAT/Pets protocols remain unchanged; the latter were already documented in v2's appendix.

E4.justification: The transfer-generalization analysis reports the opposite transfer direction, and the last-layer/all-layer controls examining feature selection disappear. Most analyses remain intact, including scaling, classifier and layer ablations, noise robustness, and online learning. The token-position ablation moves unchanged from v2 Table 2c to v3 Table 5a; qualitative success/failure examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds and means with standard deviations for SAVs and MTV in the identical appendix Table 4b. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices are introduced.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial benchmark and baseline results while retaining SAV scores on the original Table 1 tasks. LLaVA-OV LoRA changes from 44.9 to 78.3 on MHaluBench and from 43.8 to 90.0 on VLGuard without documenting a setting revision. Transfer results are replaced under a different source condition, not improved under identical conditions. New gain rows include errors: Qwen NaturalBench-retrieval group scores of 42.5 versus 35.6 imply +6.9, but v3 prints +13.8.

T1.justification: The attention, centroid, cosine-similarity, head-selection, and voting equations are unchanged, as is Appendix Algorithm 1. V3's local/global classifier explanation introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central finetuning-free feature-extraction, few-shot performance, scaling, and generalization claims remain. V3 relaxes the abstract/introduction sparsity claim from fewer than 1% to fewer than 5% of heads, although its conclusion still says 1%. The conclusion replaces closing the gap with encoder VLMs with closing the gap with GPT-4o.

C2.justification: V3 adds the hypothesis that instruction tuning disrupts in-context learning capabilities and that SAVs avoid this through internal activations. Its statement that ICL consistently deteriorates performance is stronger than Table 1 supports. Existing interpretations of sparsity and generalization, and limitations concerning closed models and voting-based confidence, remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 removes the project/code URL supplied after v2's abstract without providing replacement code-access information. Existing PyTorch, A100, official-model implementation, LoRA hyperparameter-source, and retained-dataset prompt disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for ImageNet, VizWiz, Flowers, CUB, Cross-Modal Adaptation, and two studies relevant to in-context learning behavior. The positioning against prompting, finetuning, task vectors, and encoder features remains largely intact despite substantial rewriting of related work.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title, substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction and related work, and systematically replaces discriminative-task terminology with vision-language classification terminology. It removes the separate Models subsection, reorganizes benchmark descriptions, and rearranges material between the main text and supplement.

P2.justification: Table 1 is extensively redesigned with additional task groups, vertical headings, baseline rows, and green gain rows. Figure 3 is redrawn with different colors, axes, legends, and embedding displays. The ablation and supplementary-result tables are reorganized, including the token-position and few-shot SigLIP moves. Figures 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6 retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: The added retrieval and answerability evaluations, together with the Cross-Modal Adaptation comparison, more directly test the claimed value of joint multimodal features and strengthen empirical support. The net gain is limited by removal of last-layer/all-layer controls and code-access information, unexplained LoRA score revisions, and arithmetic errors in the new gain rows. The core mathematical and uncertainty evidence remains unchanged.
